newsitem.title: INDIA: Singapore sees good prospects for Indian reforms.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sees good prospects for Indian reforms.

text.p: The long-term prospects for India's economic reforms are good despite some hitches in the recent past, Singapore Minister for Information and the Arts George Yeo said on Friday.

"The long-term climate for economic reform in India is good. This has been powerfully reinforced by Minister Chidambaram's recent budget," Yeo, who is also junior Trade and Industry Minister, told an international business conference.
Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram slashed corporate and personal taxes and cut customs duties in his budget proposals for 1997/98 (April-March) presented on February 28.

Yeo said Singapore International Airlines (SIA) had begun to take a calm approach to continuing confusion in the Indian government over approval for a two-year-old $500-million plan to set up a domestic airline with India's Tata group.
Industry Minister Murasoli Maran has supported the proposal, while Civil Aviation Minister Chand Mahal Ibrahim has opposed the move. A final decision has not yet been taken.

"Afer a few years, SIA is no longer easily excited or disappointed. Foreigners who engage in the affairs of India learn eventually to take a certain philosophical approach at the pace and rhythm of change, if for no other reason than to comfort themselves," Yeo said.

But there could be no doubt that things were changing, he said. "As reforms gather momentum, those who stand in the way will eventually be swept aside...There will be meanders but the force of change is unstoppable."
As of July 1996, Singaporean companies had invested about $600 million in 200 projects in India, Yeo said.
India began wooing foreign investors under a free market-oriented economic reform programme launched in 1991.
